meetings.title: Finance Quarterly Budget Review
meetings.summary_text: The first-quarter FY27 budget review found operating spend about two and a half percent over budget, driven mainly by travel, which ran at 180 thousand against a budget of 90 thousand. Ravi decided to freeze discretionary travel until the thirty-first of January, with already-booked client-facing trips allowed to proceed. Actions were assigned for the manager notice, the executive briefing, the revised forecast and the reconciliation of September card statements, while the expense tool and any release of contingency were not taken forward.

narrative.text: The first-quarter FY27 budget review found operating spend about two and a half percent over budget, driven mainly by travel, which ran at 180 thousand against a budget of 90 thousand.
Ravi decided to freeze discretionary travel until the thirty-first of January, with already-booked client-facing trips allowed to proceed.

Actions were assigned for the manager notice, the executive briefing, the revised forecast and the reconciliation of September card statements, while the expense tool and any release of contingency were not taken forward.

decisions.text: Discretionary travel is frozen until the thirty-first of January; client-facing trips already booked can go ahead, and other travel needs Ravi's approval.
Contingency stays at five percent for now.
The expense tool that reads receipts automatically will wait for next year's budget round.

highlights.text: Travel overspend was about half from the Brisbane client workshops, which were approved in July; the rest came from project teams.
About forty September card transactions lack receipts, mostly from the Brisbane trip, and must be fixed before the auditors arrive.
Hannah noted the contingency may be needed for the Atlas contractor.

action_items.description: Send a short notice to all managers explaining the travel freeze
Brief the executive team on the travel freeze
Rebuild and send the revised full-year forecast with the travel freeze and slipped renewals
Chase missing receipts and reconcile September corporate card statements

meetings.title: Service Desk Improvement Meeting
meetings.summary_text: The service desk meeting aimed to reduce the backlog before year end, since last month about 800 tickets were opened and 740 closed. The team agreed to rewrite the outdated password reset article, pursue about ten loan laptops pending finance approval, and introduce a daily triage rota starting next Monday. Several follow-up tasks were assigned, including tidying the shared mailbox rules, checking the remote support licence count, and taking the approval request to Ravi.

narrative.text: The service desk meeting aimed to reduce the backlog before year end, since last month about 800 tickets were opened and 740 closed.
The team agreed to rewrite the outdated password reset article, pursue about ten loan laptops pending finance approval, and introduce a daily triage rota starting next Monday.
Several follow-up tasks were assigned, including tidying the shared mailbox rules, checking the remote support licence count, and taking the approval request to Ravi.

decisions.text: The password reset knowledge base article will be rewritten.
Ten loan laptops will be ordered once finance approves the request.
A daily triage rota, with one person each morning sorting the queue, will be introduced and start next Monday.

highlights.text: Password resets are the biggest ticket category, about a quarter of everything, and many could be handled through the self-service page that people do not know about.
The vendor has already agreed to a service credit for the email gateway outage, so Lena's planned request is no longer needed.
Alex Morgan noted that finance asked whether a loan pool would save money or just move the cost, and Marcus argued it would save money.

action_items.description: Rewrite the password reset knowledge base article and put the new version up
Tidy up the shared mailbox rules so access requests reach the right queue
Order the loan laptops once finance approval comes through
Take the loan laptop approval request to Ravi and report when it is signed
Draft the triage rota and send it round so it can start next Monday
Check the remote support tool licence count against new starters

meetings.title: Level Four Fit-out Check-in
meetings.summary_text: Owen chaired the weekly check-in on the level four fit-out with Brendan from Northgate Fitouts, who reported demolition finished, the ceiling grid in, electricians starting Monday, and the floor still due back in the third week of November. The team discussed a power variation to raise the desk power points from four to six per bank, costing roughly four thousand dollars, and agreed Brendan would send revised drawings by Monday before Priya signs off. Following staff complaints about noise on level three, the team agreed noisy work moves to after six in the evening, the quiet room stays open, and facilities will deliver and label crates before the move.

meetings.title: Graduate Recruitment Planning
meetings.summary_text: The graduate recruitment planning meeting reviewed about three hundred applications for next year's intake, which closed on Friday. The team agreed to offer six places, as set in the workforce plan, and set out the shortlisting, technical exercise, assessment day and interview timetable. A paid internship for candidates who narrowly miss out was parked because there is no budget for it this year.

highlights.text: Last year's technical exercise leaked online, and last year's took most people three hours against a one-hour target.
Rooms three and four were already reserved for the assessment day on the twelfth of November.

action_items.description: Do a first-pass screen of written answers down to about forty candidates
Write a new one-hour technical exercise for the engineering stream
Confirm the interview panel members
Coordinate catering for the assessment day
Write a one-page interviewing guide and send it to the panel

meetings.title: Customer Complaint Escalation Review
meetings.summary_text: The review covered three escalated complaints, starting with Mrs Delaney, who was charged twice for her subscription and had not been told the refund had gone through. The team agreed that a wrong phone number on about two thousand brochures would be reprinted by Coastal Print at their cost by the sixth of November, with a website correction going up the same day. Refund approval was identified as part of the problem, and the team agreed that refunds up to five hundred dollars can now be approved by the team leader. The complaints register is to be updated with all three cases before the quarterly audit, and the escalation threshold will go on the agenda for the next monthly meeting.

decisions.text: Refunds up to five hundred dollars can be approved by the team leader; only refunds over five hundred dollars need a manager.
The complaints register will have all three cases added before the quarterly audit.
The escalation threshold itself will be reviewed at the next monthly meeting.

highlights.text: The third complaint, a customer who waited forty minutes on hold, has been resolved and the customer was called back.
Coastal Print have already apologised for the wrong phone number on the brochures.

action_items.description: Call Mrs Delaney back and apologise
Draft apology letter for Mrs Delaney and get it to Priya for signing
Reprint brochures with corrected phone number
Put correction on the website
Add all three cases to the complaints register and tidy it
Put escalation threshold review on the agenda for the next monthly meeting

meetings.title: Quarterly All-Staff Briefing
meetings.summary_text: The quarterly all-staff briefing was an information session covering the office move, first-quarter results, and Project Atlas, followed by online questions. The Collins Street office is on schedule, with level four finished in the third week of November and the move on the weekend of the twenty-eighth. Revenue was eleven point six million, three percent ahead of plan, and the travel freeze is in place until the end of January. The steering committee moved the Project Atlas go-live date to the fourteenth of December, and the mobile app will follow in the new year. Briefings will now be held every two months instead of every quarter, with the next one in the new office in January.

The Collins Street office is on schedule, with level four finished in the third week of November and the move on the weekend of the twenty-eighth.
Revenue was eleven point six million, three percent ahead of plan, and the travel freeze is in place until the end of January.
The steering committee moved the Project Atlas go-live date to the fourteenth of December, and the mobile app will follow in the new year.
Briefings will now be held every two months instead of every quarter, with the next one in the new office in January.

decisions.text: The Project Atlas go-live date moved from the thirtieth of November to the fourteenth of December, and the mobile app is no longer part of the first release.
Briefings will be held every two months instead of every quarter.

highlights.text: Customer retention was ninety-one percent, the best quarter in two years.
October's travel spend was less than half of September's since the freeze began.
Approved conferences before the travel freeze are unaffected; the freeze applies only to new discretionary travel.
The Atlas delay does not affect the customer launch event, which remains planned for February.

meetings.title: Project Atlas Steering Committee
meetings.summary_text: The steering committee met to decide whether to keep the thirtieth of November go-live, given that data migration for historical invoices was still unfinished and testing needed more time. The committee agreed to move go-live to the fourteenth of December, accepting a roughly twenty-thousand-dollar contractor extension, and to remove the mobile app from the first release. Actions were assigned across migration scripts, regression testing, the contract extension, release notes, the board presentation, the payments adapter, search performance and user acceptance testing.

meetings.title: Health and Safety Committee
meetings.summary_text: The health and safety committee reviewed two October incidents, a fire drill that is overdue, first-aid kit and officer gaps, and a proposal on meeting frequency. The committee agreed to replace the broken level-two exit sign, enter both incidents in the register, run the fire drill on the twentieth, recruit first-aid officers, and meet monthly until the move is complete.

meetings.title: Customer Success Retrospective Q3
meetings.summary_text: The Q3 customer success retrospective reviewed what went well and what did not, and agreed a set of changes for the coming quarter. Renewals went well at ninety-one percent and the new onboarding checklist cut time to first value by about a week, while the CRM sync failure and late churn warnings were the main problems. The team agreed to send renewal lists to account managers eight weeks ahead, and to move the NPS survey to quarterly.
